4fFDFbi3toc.title: "Testing Distributed Systems w/ Deterministic Simulation" by Will Wilson
4fFDFbi3toc.summary: Will Wilson of FoundationDB explains how the team tested their distributed database using deterministic simulation. By running the whole system in a simulator with injected faults and reproducible seeds, they could find rare concurrency and network bugs.
4fFDFbi3toc.why_hn: HN treats it as the canonical talk on simulation testing and a mind-blowing example of how far rigorous testing can go.

quote.text: this is one of the most amazing talks on distributed systems

yCcWpzY8dIA.title: Conflict Resolution for Eventual Consistency • Martin Kleppmann • GOTO 2016
yCcWpzY8dIA.summary: Martin Kleppmann's GOTO Berlin 2016 talk on how collaborative editors, offline apps, and multi-datacenter databases handle concurrent updates. It covers conflict resolution approaches including operational transformation and CRDTs, with a worked look at text CRDTs.
yCcWpzY8dIA.why_hn: Treated as the go-to approachable yet deep primer on CRDTs and collaborative editing, recommended repeatedly in threads on Automerge, local-first software and OT versus CRDT.

quote.text: Rest of the talk is also highly recommended for anyone interested in an approachable primer on CRDTs.

m64SWl9bfvk.title: "Stop Rate Limiting! Capacity Management Done Right" by Jon Moore
m64SWl9bfvk.summary: Jon Moore's Strange Loop 2017 talk argues that rate limiting is the wrong tool for protecting services from noisy clients. He proposes concurrency-based capacity management and quotas instead.
m64SWl9bfvk.why_hn: HN engineers recommend it for its core insight that limiting concurrency naturally yields request-rate limits, and for its link to queueing theory.

quote.text: The basic premise is not do do req/s limiting but rather concurrency limiting which results in req/s limiting by itself.

EY6q5dv_B-o.title: VCF East: Ken Thompson interviewed by Brian Kernighan
EY6q5dv_B-o.summary: Brian Kernighan interviews Unix co-creator Ken Thompson at VCF East 2019. Thompson recounts how he was hired at Bell Labs, writing the Unix kernel in about three weeks, the origins of B and TMG, pipes, and other anecdotes.
EY6q5dv_B-o.why_hn: HN commenters recommend it for Thompson's funny, first-hand Unix history stories, some of which even Kernighan had not heard.

-zRN7XLCRhc.title: LISA11 - Fork Yeah! The Rise and Development of illumos
-zRN7XLCRhc.summary: Bryan Cantrill's LISA11 talk on how illumos arose after Oracle closed OpenSolaris. It covers the history of Sun, ZFS, DTrace and Zones, and the diaspora of kernel engineers, with a famous rant about Oracle and Larry Ellison.
-zRN7XLCRhc.why_hn: HN points to it as the definitive, entertaining account of Sun's fate under Oracle, and quotes its Ellison lawnmower advice whenever Oracle behaves badly.

quote.text: If you're interested how it came to be check out this epic talk by Bryan Cantrill

o_AIw9bGogo.title: The Tragedy of systemd
o_AIw9bGogo.summary: FreeBSD developer Benno Rice traces the history of init and bootstrap systems at linux.conf.au 2019 to explain why systemd was seen as necessary and why it provokes such strong reactions. He also discusses why change is scary.
o_AIw9bGogo.why_hn: The most-recommended balanced take on systemd, from a BSD perspective, handed to anyone caught up in the systemd debate.

quote.text: is an interesting talk on this topic from the view of someone (Benno Rice) in BSD land. Highly recommended.

fU9hR3kiOK0.title: "Turning the database inside out with Apache Samza" by Martin Kleppmann
fU9hR3kiOK0.summary: Martin Kleppmann argues that databases are global shared mutable state and proposes treating them as an ever-growing log of immutable facts. Derived data such as caches, indexes and views is then built by stream processors like Apache Samza. The talk draws on Kafka and LinkedIn's experience with commit logs.
fU9hR3kiOK0.why_hn: Commenters repeatedly cite it as the talk that reframed how they think about caching, derived data and event sourcing.

quote.text: This talk on Apache Samza completely changed how I think about caching and derived data in general

NVl9_6J1G60.title: Breakout Session Presented by Dan Robinson of Heap at PGConf Silicon Valley 2015
NVl9_6J1G60.summary: Dan Robinson, then CTO of Heap, explains how Heap runs its product analytics backend on PostgreSQL and CitusDB. It covers conversion funnels, retention and cohort queries across tens of billions of events and 50 TB of data, plus Postgres and Kafka together and the indexing strategy.
NVl9_6J1G60.why_hn: HN commenters point to it as a first-hand overview of Heap's Postgres/Citus architecture and its distinctive indexing approach.

quote.text: Dan from Heap Analytics has a great talk about how they use Postgres and Citus.

xNzoerDljjo.title: Saša Jurić - Parsing from first principles - WebCamp Zagreb 2019
xNzoerDljjo.summary: Sasa Juric explains how to parse a language from first principles without regexes, live-coding a simple parser combinator library in Elixir. It was given at WebCamp Zagreb 2019.
xNzoerDljjo.why_hn: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, dense hour on parsers and parser combinators that holds the audience.

quote.text: Saša Jurić is fantastic at condensing lots of information in a 1 hour talk without losing the audience
